extracted.intended_audience: editors and publishers of scientific journals, researchers, funders, bibliometric and informatics experts, information innovators, librarians, journalists, policymakers, ethicists, scientific information disseminators, and anyone interested in the scientific information enterprise and quality of scientific evidence
extracted.subtask_description: Information page for the International Peer Review Congress describing the topics and goals for research submissions and participation, focused on evidence about peer review and scientific publication practices and integrity. Useful for prospective presenters, researchers, and stakeholders in scholarly communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: quality, integrity, and credibility of peer review and scientific publication
rubrics_metrics.description: The Congress aims to "encourage research into the quality, integrity, and credibility of peer review and scientific publication."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This cluster is the primary overarching focus of the Congress: work should address one or more aspects of quality, integrity, or credibility in peer review and publication.

rubrics_metrics.name: establish the evidence base to improve conduct, reporting, and dissemination
rubrics_metrics.description: To "establish the evidence base on which scientists can improve the conduct, reporting, and dissemination of scientific research."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Submissions should contribute empirical or theoretical evidence that can be used to improve how research is conducted, reported, and disseminated.

rubrics_metrics.name: editorial and funding peer review
rubrics_metrics.description: Presentation and discussion of research into "editorial and funding peer review."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes studies of review processes conducted by journals and by funders; evaluations of review models and their effects on decision-making and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: scientific and scholarly publication
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses work on publication practices, policies, editorial workflows, and the lifecycle of scholarly outputs.

rubrics_metrics.name: research and reporting practices
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Addresses methods, standards, and norms for how research is designed, conducted, and reported; may include reporting guidelines and compliance studies.

rubrics_metrics.name: identification and management of biases
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on the "identification and management of biases."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes detection of bias in review, publication, authorship, citation, and editorial decisions, and interventions or policies to mitigate such biases.

rubrics_metrics.name: transparency
rubrics_metrics.description: Work addressing "transparency" in peer review and publication.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers transparency of processes (e.g., open peer review), reporting of methods and results, disclosure practices, and data/code availability.

rubrics_metrics.name: reproducibility
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses reproducibility/replicability studies, reproducible workflows, and assessments of how publication and review practices affect reproducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: access
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pertains to open access, equitable access to research outputs, barriers to access, and implications for dissemination and use.

rubrics_metrics.name: publication and dissemination metrics
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Includes bibliometrics, altmetrics, measures of impact, and critiques or validation of metrics used to evaluate publications and researchers.

rubrics_metrics.name: identification and management of threats to the integrity of science
rubrics_metrics.description: Research on the "identification and management of threats to the integrity of science."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Covers misconduct, questionable research practices, fraud detection, retractions, and systems or policies to protect scientific integrity.

rubrics_metrics.name: advances in information exchange
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Encompasses technological, procedural, and policy innovations for sharing, curating, and disseminating scientific information (e.g., platforms, standards, interoperability).
